title: Circumcision
what: A surgeon removes the foreskin. This is the skin that covers the head of the penis. The skin edges are closed with stitches that dissolve.
why: For medical reasons, such as a tight foreskin or frequent inflammation. Also for religious or family tradition.
duration: the surgery usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners
If anyone in your family has bleeding problems
If you, your child, or relatives ever had problems with anesthesia
If your child recently had a cold or a fever

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: Adults usually get local anesthesia. Children often get general anesthesia. The doctor decides.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests are usually needed. Sometimes a check by a pediatrician or a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If you will have general anesthesia, do not eat or drink for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Take a shower the day before. For a child, bring comfortable loose underwear or diapers.

bring: Your ID. For a child, the birth certificate
steps: You or your child change into a gown
Pain relief is given: a shot at the base of the penis, or general anesthesia
The skin edges are closed with thin stitches that dissolve
You are watched for a short time and then go home
feel: With local anesthesia: a prick, then only touch
After surgery: burning and pain, especially when you pee. You will get pain medicine
after: Swelling and redness usually last a few days. This is normal
Care for the wound and dressing as your doctor tells you
The stitches usually dissolve in 1 to 3 weeks
Wear loose underwear, no tight clothes
Adults: usually no sex for 4 to 6 weeks. Check with your doctor
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop when you press on it
You cannot pee for more than 6 to 8 hours
A fever over 38 degrees, or swelling, redness, or pus that gets worse
The head of the penis turns dark or bluish: see a doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.q: What is the best age for circumcision?
faq.a: It can be done at any age. A pediatric surgeon or urologist will help you choose the age and type of pain relief.

faq.q: How long does it take to heal?
faq.a: Usually 2 to 3 weeks. Swelling goes down in a few days, and the stitches dissolve on their own.

reminders.text: Circumcision tomorrow. Bring your ID, test results, and loose underwear. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
